source.provider: Purdue Geospatial Data Science Lab / Indiana Digital Forestry
source.title: Indiana 2017–2019 3DEP LiDAR Normalized Digital Height Model
source.tile_georeferencing: Upper-left (2,995,000, 1,890,000) ftUS; rows increase south, columns increase east.

footprint.transform: EPSG:4326 to EPSG:2968 with pyproj; cell center samples tested inside projected polygon.

method.sampling: Raster cell centers inside the official CQE polygon; nearest cell value, no interpolation.
method.likely_roof_screen: 25–65 ftUS above ground, an analysis choice informed by the neighborhood distribution to exclude near-ground/mixed edge cells and extreme values; raw values are preserved below.
method.neighbor_check: All raster cells outside the polygon and inside a 10-cell (50 ft) bounding-box buffer.
method.uncertainty: Five-foot cells mix roof, ground, and overhanging canopy near edges. The raster is a normalized surface model, not a measured elevation survey. Screening and polygon geometry affect statistics; height quantiles support only an approximate surface-height range, not floor count or eave/ridge height individually.
